title: PGSQL: Dissect CopyData content
description:
PostgreSQL uses CopyData messages for replication streams. Messages like
keepalives, standby and hot standby feedback updates are sent in a
CopyData message. Additionally, logical replication is sent through
XLogData messages within a CopyData.

CopyData messages are described in https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-replication.html#PROTOCOL-REPLICATION-START-REPLICATION
Logical replication messages are described in https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-logicalrep-message-formats.html

This patch adds dissection for the CopyData details and the content of
XLogData if logical replication messages are detected.

added 17 commits
  • 30211056...b6ddd18e - 16 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 836bb7cf - PGSQL: Dissect CopyData content
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20268/diffs?diff_id=1396719175&start_sha=3021105656f7c1895c4b861162295e7b742125a1)

The documentation suggests that this field is only available from protocol version 2 and later:

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-logicalrep-message-formats.html

Does it need a check on `proto_version`? (Similar in other messages)
Or is it sufficient because `is_streamed_txn` is only set by messages that are present in version 2 and later?

Yes, streamed transactions were introduced with `proto_version` 2. Message descriptions like "Xid of the transaction (only present for streamed transactions). This field is available since protocol version 2." is a bit redundant since a streamed transaction is always going to be with a `proto_version` >=2.

I've also avoided the check to make specifying the `proto_version` as optional as possible. If we detect a streamed transaction, then those messages must have the xid field.

Since this is at the end of the message, is it not possible to use a message length somewhere to decide if this is present, so that a user would not have to configure the `proto_version` manually as a preference?

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20268/diffs?diff_id=1397255486&start_sha=836bb7cfee0d0661aba17e0197e0f4447a1a8018#773a32a360fee9f02b82536b3e050829d3a06926_698_697)

Good point. Also, looking more into Postgres' behaviour, it turns out that the doc is confusing as it suggests that messages with `proto_version=4` will have the abort LSN and TS.

But PG will only send it if [streaming was set to parallel](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/4464fddf7b50abe3dbb462f76fd925e10eedad1c/src/backend/replication/pgoutput/pgoutput.c#L1874). So it's possible to use `proto_version` 4 and not have the abort info.

I've changed the check to only rely on length which makes the `proto_version` parameter unnecessary.
Great.

Is `proto_version` 1 the most useful default for the preference? The preference appears to make no change in behavior beyond "less than 4" and "4 and greater?" Do recent versions of PostgreSQL default to a later version, or version 1, (or must it be specified in each command?)

It's up to the client to decide and I've mostly seen clients using `proto_version` 1 as a safe default. Higher `proto_version` requires to be sure the server supports the requested version. ([Debezium](https://github.com/debezium/debezium/blob/78ae91d6b1e3215496623279371114be3177311d/debezium-connector-postgres/src/main/java/io/debezium/connector/postgresql/connection/pgoutput/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java#L232) for example is hardcoded to use `proto_version` 1.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20268/diffs?diff_id=1397255486&start_sha=836bb7cfee0d0661aba17e0197e0f4447a1a8018#773a32a360fee9f02b82536b3e050829d3a06926_155_155)
It might be helpful to extend the longer description (used for tooltips, etc.) to mention what values are possible and currently supported by the dissector.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20268/diffs?diff_id=1397255486&start_sha=836bb7cfee0d0661aba17e0197e0f4447a1a8018#773a32a360fee9f02b82536b3e050829d3a06926_2180_2180)
The `proto_version` is now deleted.
Do you have a sample capture for this feature, that could be used for fuzz testing?
